LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD for `ttcli` is a standard Go packaging script. During `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, only the global/top-level scope is sourced — this includes comments and variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `optdepends`, `conflicts`, `source`, `sha256sums`). None of these execute code; they are plain assignments, and the `${pkgname}`/`${pkgver}` expansions in the `source` array merely produce a static upstream tarball URL. There are no top-level command substitutions (e.g. `$(...)`, backticks), no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget` invocations, and no data exfiltration attempts.

The `source` array points to the package's own upstream repository (`github.com/j4y-w4lk3r/ttcli`), which is expected upstream behavior. A valid `sha256sums` entry is present (not SKIP), though as noted, checksum handling is out of scope for this gate anyway. The `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions are never executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so their contents are out of scope for this specific gate and will be audited separately. No backdoors, reverse shells, or unexpected file operations exist in the global scope.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard Go PKGBUILD; safe to source for SRCINFO generation.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
